source.title: Inferior olive oscillation as the temporal basis for motricity and oscillatory reset as the basis for motor error correction

confidence_rationale: A canonical, mechanistically detailed review by the investigator who characterised the inferior olive's subthreshold oscillation and electrotonic coupling, and it directly evidences the specific biophysical substrate ARC-053's own notes name first. Downweighted from the source quality it would otherwise earn because it is a review advancing a particular theoretical position rather than a single controlled test, and because the domain is motor timing rather than the perceptual prediction/input coupling ARC-053 cares about.
failure_signatures: The mechanism is demonstrated for motor sequencing and motor error correction; the paper offers no evidence that inferior olive phase reset governs coupling between descending predictions and ascending input in perceptual or imaginative modes.

The 1-10 Hz olivary oscillation is a slow timing signal. If REE's V(t) phase-alignment term ends up requiring alignment at gamma-band or faster timescales, this substrate is the wrong frequency and the connectome hypothesis in ARC-053's notes would need revision rather than support.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Inferior olivary neurons are electrotonically coupled and generate subthreshold membrane-potential oscillations at 1-10 Hz that impose a common temporal frame on distributed motor commands; the same circuitry can rapidly RESET oscillatory phase, and this reset is proposed as the substrate for on-line motor error correction.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-053's notes name 'inferior olive + cerebellum + thalamus + cortical networks (MECH-226)' as the biophysical substrate hypothesis for the TCL. This paper is the primary evidence for the olivary leg of that hypothesis, and it supplies something the thalamic literature does not: an explicit PHASE-RESET operation. That maps onto TCL function (2) 'adjusts timing windows and synchrony' -- the TCL is not only a passive clock but something that can be re-aligned on the basis of error, which is precisely what a control loop maintaining coherence would need.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The entire demonstration is in the motor domain -- timing of movement and correction of movement error. ARC-053 asserts a coherence loop in service of a verisimilitude readout over prediction/input coupling, which is a perceptual and cross-modal claim. Importing the olivary mechanism into that role is an architectural ANALOGY (an error-driven phase-reset controller is what the TCL would need to be), not a measured finding. There is also a frequency-band commitment hidden in the transfer: 1-10 Hz.
mapping.source_context: Review of in vitro and in vivo rodent and cat inferior olive electrophysiology, synthesised into a theoretical account of olivo-cerebellar timing; single-author position paper.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.75: authoritative and mechanistically specific, but a theory-advancing review rather than a controlled test, and the olivo-cerebellar timing hypothesis remains contested in parts of the cerebellar literature. Mapping fidelity 0.60: it evidences the named substrate and supplies the phase-reset primitive, but in the wrong task domain. Transfer risk 0.45 is the highest of this pull -- motor-to-perceptual transfer plus an implicit frequency-band commitment. Aggregate reflects that this entry supports the SUBSTRATE hypothesis in ARC-053's notes more than it supports ARC-053's core assertion.
